thesis: The shipped ladder (ladder-qld-schd, QLD/SCHD/IEF) trades exactly the three tickers a taxable momentum or income strategy is most likely to also want, which is disqualifying for a Roth IRA: Rev. Rul. 2008-5 holds that a loss sold in a taxable account and replaced inside an IRA within 30 days is disallowed with no basis adjustment anywhere, strictly worse than an ordinary wash sale, which only defers the loss. `backend/app/tax/washsale.py` models the destruction; the cheaper fix is never letting the two accounts name the same ticker at all (strategy-program/THREE-PURPOSES-PLAN.md section 6). This card re-expresses the identical mechanism -- same signal, same rungs, same confirmation gate, same recovery clock, same fund-order (bond before defensive) -- on three tickers disjoint from the original: QLD (2x Nasdaq-100, ProShares) becomes SSO (2x S&P 500, ProShares) -- same leverage factor, a genuinely different underlying index, not a relabelling of the same one; SCHD (Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index) becomes VIG (S&P U.S. Dividend Growers Index, Vanguard) -- a different provider and a different selection philosophy, dividend growth rather than high current yield; IEF (ICE U.S. Treasury 7-10 Year Index) becomes BND (Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate Bond Index, Vanguard) -- broader than Treasuries alone, adding investment-grade corporate and mortgage-backed exposure, a real change in what the bond sleeve is actually exposed to, not merely a different duration bucket of the same collateral. None of this is a claim that the substitution satisfies IRC section 1091's substantially-identical test -- the IRS has never ruled on ETF pairs of this kind, and strategy-program/ROTH-DISJOINT-LADDER.md says explicitly that ticker disjointness is a necessary condition this card satisfies, not a sufficient one the backtest can prove. The signal stays SPY, unchanged and untraded, because the drawdown trigger is a fact about the broad market's own price level, not a position either account holds. This would be falsified by: (a) the substitute tickers' longer or shorter histories changing which regimes the backtest can even see, most importantly whether SCHD's own 2011-10-20 start (not any substitute's) remains the binding constraint on the shared comparison window; (b) evidence that SSO, VIG or BND individually correlates with its QLD/SCHD/IEF counterpart closely enough that the substitution changes nothing real about the strategy's risk profile, which would undercut the same-strategy claim in the opposite direction from the section-1091 concern; or (c) the contribution-funded backtest in strategy-program/tools/roth_disjoint.py showing the substitution costs enough on IRR, CAGR or MAR that holding this strategy on disjoint tickers is not worth the tax protection it buys -- see that script's own report for the measured number, not a claim made here in advance of running it.
